about: An invented learner for tests and evals. Not based on any real person.
summary: IELTS Academic 7.5 by 12 Dec 2026. Portuguese first language, lives in Lisbon, works 9 to 6. Google Calendar. 60-minute sessions on 4 days a week, before work and on Saturday mornings.
first_message: I need a 7.5 in IELTS Academic by December for my master's offer. Can you set me up and keep me honest?

replies.reply: 12 December, the paper-based test, starting at 9:00. I'm not registered yet; I have to register by 20 October. Listening, reading and writing are 2 h 45 min together, speaking is separate. No calculator, no reference sheet, no extra time.

Around 6.0, I think. Reading is the weakest, especially matching headings. I did one practice test at home in September and reading came out around band 6, but I looked some words up during it. I have no official score and no item-level report.

Cambridge IELTS 18: I've done tests 1 and 2. Two official practice tests from the test provider that I haven't opened. No solutions booklet. For theory, use Cambridge IELTS 18's examples; I don't have a grammar book.

replies.about: age band, first language, feedback tone
replies.reply: 18+. Portuguese is my first language. B.
60 minutes, 4 days a week. 90 at the very most.

replies.about: windows, clearest time, sleep, fixed-time preferences
replies.reply: Before work on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday, 7:00 to 8:15, and Saturday 10 to 12. My head is clearest early in the morning. I sleep 23:30 to 6:30 on work nights, a bit later at weekends. I'd like Saturdays for the longer timed practice.
Work 9 to 6 on weekdays. A friend's wedding on Saturday 17 October, the whole day. Sunday is my day off. What stopped me before: a busy month at work, I skipped a week and never went back.

replies.about: two-week plan preview and calendar choice
replies.reply: Looks good. 1, and put them in a separate calendar called Study.

later_answers.P6: Work ran late and I missed it.

later_phrases.missed: I missed Thursday, work ran over

expected.match_note: Ids, enums, numbers, dates and times are compared exactly. Free-text values (goal, why, success, notes, what) are compared by meaning, not wording. Objects inside lists are compared on the keys given.

Do not calibrate on: the September practice test (words were looked up during it)
Learner notes: Clearest early in the morning, before work
Wants Saturdays for longer timed practice
If work gets busy, then keep the 2-day rechecks and shorten the rest rather than skipping a week

readback_mentions: 60 min × 4 days, about 4 h a week, ceiling about 6 h
Google Calendar, a calendar called Study, ask before each batch
hard words explained in Portuguese the first time
answers on paper, sent as phone photos; no printer needed
the two unopened official tests: a checkpoint on 14 Nov and the final mock on 21 Nov
what's tested: the published format, with 'say if any is missing' (no separate question)
checks: No file exists in the workspace before the readback 'yes'.
Session length, days per week and the calendar choice are all settled before any plan is written.
At most one question card per message; the reply count is at most max_replies.
Q1 is not asked: the opener echoes the first message (IELTS Academic 7.5, December, master's offer) and starts at Q2; the floor defaults to 7.0.
The plan preview carries one rough-fit line labelled [mine] (every topic counted at mastery 0 until the diagnostic).
A dated to-do records the registration deadline (20 Oct 2026).
Nothing is planned on 2026-10-17 (wedding), inside working hours, or within 30 minutes of bedtime; nothing goes on a Sunday without asking.
The diagnostic comes before any teaching and sits in the clear morning window.
Every 2-day recheck is planned 44 to 72 hours after its teach; when the wedding and the rest day make that impossible, Claude moves the teach or asks, and never serves the recheck outside its window.

The two unopened official practice tests are kept for measurement and never used as practice: materials.ration gives official test 1 to a checkpoint on 2026-11-14 and official test 2 to the final mock on 2026-11-21, so the diagnostic is Claude-built.
Calendar events are written only after the preview and option 1, and are read back afterwards.
Learner-facing text contains no E-, B-, S- or L- ids, no answers and no emojis.
